critic: LEAD (independent critic, checked by a second agent)
verdict:
C19: evidence_table at f720f32. The pair camera is now a usable compositing plate, but the stage is still not at pro level.

What I reviewed:
- pair.png was committed in f720f32 at 09:56. 190c7d0 added optics and depth data to pair.corners.json and changed nothing else in it.
- Two newer commits are on the remote branch but not in this checkout, so I did not see them:
  - 570728f has pair.mask.png.
  - 64abcff has a 2560 screen render and screen.corners.json.
- Every other published frame is out of date:
  - page.jpg is from 09:22. It still shows the khaki marker and the pair's pen. The new highlighter, page pen and boards from 8deb50b (10:11) exist only in code.
  - screen is the 1280x720 render from 07:54.
  - overhead, push, laptop, purses and passport are the 04:54 renders (7249565), regraded with A fixed at 06:14.

All pair measurements below are on the raw 2560x1440 frame.

The P1 failures from r6 are fixed:
- The cushioned edges, dark rims and rounded corners are gone.
- The pen no longer touches document_left. It is about 22 mm away at the cap end and about 50 mm at the tip.
- The paper has no texture: high-pass std is 0.40 on both sheets.
- Graded pixels below luma 8 are 0.19% of the frame.

The pins are good:
- Every corner is within 1.1 px of the visible corner.
- Every visible edge sits 0.17-0.74 px outside its pinned line.
- That offset is largest on the two out-of-focus top edges, which is what you get from measuring a blurred edge at half its brightness on gamma-encoded values. The true errors are probably smaller.
- The compositor multiplies a page with white margins into the plate, so a sliver of blank paper outside the page cannot be seen.
- Tracking is ready.

The right sheet is darker because of lamp falloff, not because it is a different paper:
- On the raw, luma runs on across the gap: about 187 at the left sheet's right edge and about 182 at the right sheet's left edge.
- At matched luma (178-190) the colour is the same within 0.01: r/g 1.104 against 1.111, b/g 0.878 against 0.869.
- The darker sheet is a little warmer, which is what bounce light off the wood would do.

What still gets in the way of a pinned page:

(1) A soft shadow wedge sits on document_left's top-left corner, with nothing in frame to cause it.
- Raw luma there is 152 at 5x5 mm in, against 191 at 30x30 mm and about 197-204 farther in.
- The 3 mm/20 mm ratio is 0.918 at the top-edge station nearest the corner and 0.938 on the left edge.
- The code's geometry points to the soft edge of the lamp's spot cone:
  - SPOT has no 'plate' entry, so set_lamp() gives pair the 72-degree, blend-0.70 cone. It is at full strength only within about 19.5 degrees of its axis.
  - This corner is about 29 degrees off the axis, at roughly 0.45 strength. Every other corner of both sheets is within about 25 degrees.
- Next to it, a dark rounded shape with a curved edge fills the frame's top-left corner (the old lamp-base arc).
  - The wood there is raw 25-30, against about 37-53 elsewhere.
  - The lamp base stands at (-0.35, 0.20), just outside that corner of the frame. A base 8 cm across reaches about 170 px into the frame.
  - For 'plate' the lamp meshes are hidden from the camera but still cast shadows, so the camera sees the dark table under the base.

(2) In this render the wood still looks procedural. All three problems are fixed in code but not yet rendered:
- Scratches are at 0.5. Pale near-vertical and diagonal ones run along the top band (x about 1070-2000), in the gap between the sheets and to the right of the right sheet.
- Board 2's end-joint (x = -0.17):
  - It comes down from the top of the frame (x about 510, y 0-195) to the left sheet's top edge, just right of its top-left corner. It pulls the eye to the pin.
  - It then runs on as a dark hairline within 2 mm of document_left's left edge, from about y 440 to the board seam at about y 655. At its darkest the wood is raw 17-25 at 0.5 mm out, against 74-81 at 10 mm.
  - Because it is on one edge only, it reads as a shadow line or as mis-registration.
- To the right of the right sheet, the boards below the long seam (y about 730) have tight, ruler-straight striped grain (y about 740-1060). They read as a different material from the swirled boards above.
- Board 1's end-joint (x = 0.37) is only just in frame, at x about 2550.

(3) No edge has a contact shadow, so the sheets look laid on as flat cards.
- Where the wood 10 mm out is clear of the other sheet, the wood 1 mm outside each edge is 0.81-1.16 of it.
- The only dark line hugging a sheet is the board joint in (2).

(4) The plate renders through two volumes:
- the 'table air' box (density 0.013)
- the lamp's cone_haze (density up to 0.055), whose core sits over document_left at this lamp mark.
Both add haze, and a multiplied page darkens the haze along with the paper.

(5) The graded vignette is heavy on the outer columns:
- The right sheet's right column grades about 85-107, against 153-178 on its left side.
- The left sheet's left column grades 113-140, against 159-183 on its right side.
- On the right sheet, real lamp falloff accounts for about 0.84 of the drop. The grade's vignette does the rest.
- That is heavy for a document the voice reads from. The grade (A fixed) stays as it is. Only a full-frame hold of the plate shows this, because the compositor grades its own crop.

Compared with fern's document inserts and the koi-pond stills, the paper is clean but the wood still looks like flat CG.

The stage's other seven frames are out of date, and two of them fail:
- overhead: 27.8% of graded pixels are below luma 8, with straight tone steps.
- screen: pale keys, a blotchy bezel, and only 1280 px wide.

One good plate plus code changes nobody has seen yet does not raise the stage's scores. They stay at the r6 values.
answers:
1. Scores for evidence_table at f720f32, from the published frames: see the scores. They are the same as r6:
- pair is fixed as a plate.
- page.jpg is still the 09:22 render with the khaki marker. The new marker, page pen and quieter boards from 8deb50b exist only in code.
- In this checkout, screen is still 1280x720.
- The five story cameras are still the 04:54 renders.
- I scored what is published here.
- 570728f (pair and page mattes) and 64abcff (the 2560 screen with its corners) are on the remote branch only. The review you requested at 64abcff should look at them.

2. Both page tracks.

Method:
- 120 bilinear luma profiles across each edge, at 0.1 px steps.
- The edge is where each profile crosses halfway between paper (20-40 px in) and wood (20-40 px out).
- A line is fitted to each edge: RMS 0.05-0.13 px, max 0.40.
- Corners are where neighbouring lines meet.
- Origin is the top-left pixel edge.

| Corner | Visible corner (px) | JSON pin (px) | Distance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top left | 483.03, 199.28 | 483.429, 199.865 | 0.71 px |
| Top right | 1254.31, 204.13 | 1253.706, 205.035 | 1.09 px |
| Bottom right | 1238.27, 1208.28 | 1238.184, 1207.995 | 0.30 px |
| Bottom left | 334.00, 1201.23 | 334.348, 1200.876 | 0.49 px |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Bottom left | 1281.70, 1248.18 | 1281.908, 1247.803 | 0.43 px |

- Your 0.30-1.07 px is confirmed: I get 0.25-1.09.
- Every visible edge sits outside its pinned line:
  - document_left: top +0.74, right +0.34, bottom +0.32, left +0.39 px.
  - document_right: top +0.60, right +0.17, bottom +0.31, left +0.39 px.
- The offset grows with edge softness, and the two out-of-focus top edges have the largest. A halfway crossing measured on gamma-encoded values lands about half a sigma outside the true edge, so this is mostly measurement bias, not paper thickness.
- Either way, doc_composite multiplies in a page with white margins, so that sliver is blank paper and cannot be seen.
- No pin moves onto the wood. The tracks are ready.

3. Defocus. focus_m, fstop, lens and depth_m are now in the JSON and agree with the frame.
- Edge widths, 10-90%:
  - document_left: top 2.82 px, bottom 1.56 px.
  - document_right: top 2.58 px, bottom 1.86 px.
- That fits f/6.3 focused at 0.936 m, with depths of about 1.045 m at the top and about 0.89 m at the bottom.
- The compositor still applies a flat 0.55 px GaussianBlur, so text at the top of the page will be sharper than the paper edge around it.
- In the comp, ramp sigma by depth_m:
  - in plate pixels, from about 1.0-1.1 px at the top to about 0.6-0.7 px at the bottom (the 10-90% width divided by 2.56).
  - doc_composite blurs after the warp, in output pixels, so scale the sigma by the crop's 0.75 x zoom.

4. The 3 mm and 20 mm edge samples are within 1.9% on 5 of the 8 edges, not all of them.

I took the ratio of luma 3 mm in to luma 20 mm in on the raw frame, at nine stations per edge (from 10% to 90% along it):

| Sheet | Edge | Range | Mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| document_left | Top | 0.918-0.998 | 0.976 |
| document_left | Left | 0.938-0.997 | 0.983 |
| document_left | Right | 0.986-0.994 | 0.990 |
| document_left | Bottom | 0.987-0.992 | 0.990 |
| document_right | Top | 0.981-0.999 | 0.992 |
| document_right | Right | 0.975-0.993 | 0.981 |
| document_right | Bottom | 0.989-1.000 | 0.994 |
| document_right | Left | 1.009-1.014 | 1.011 |

- document_left's top and left edges fail at their first stations (0.918 and 0.938). That is the cone-edge wedge on its top-left corner, not a rim: the 1 mm samples lie on the same smooth slope.
- document_right's right edge is just outside the limit at its top two stations (0.975-0.976, 2.5%). That is smooth falloff toward its outer side.

5. Graded paper centres: confirmed.
- Over 10x10 px at each homography centre I measure 177.2/173.7/170.3 on the left sheet and 154.1/148.8/145.0 on the right.
- Over each whole sheet, R-B averages +7.0 on the left and +9.4 on the right. Both are slightly warm, as the brief asks.

6. Is the right sheet darker because of lamp falloff or a different paper? Falloff.
- On the raw, luma steps only from about 187 at the left sheet's right edge to about 182 at the right sheet's left edge.
- At matched luma (178-190) the colour is the same within 0.01.
- The darkest corner is the right sheet's bottom right: raw about 144 at 5 mm in, against about 149 at its top right. That is the corner farthest from the lamp, which is where falloff should put it.
- The right sheet's raw falloff across its width is 187 to 149 along its top (0.80) and 182 to 153 at mid-height (0.84). On the graded full frame, the vignette makes it about 0.58.
- That is fine for pushes that crop into one page. On a full-frame hold, text in the right page's right margin will be dim.

7. Surface lighting and readiness: ready to composite. Still to fix:
- the cone-edge wedge and the lamp-base arc (fix 1)
- scratches, board end-joints and the joint hairline beside document_left (fix 2)
- no contact line (fix 3)
- haze from table air and cone_haze in the plate (fix 3)

The paper itself is excellent for a plate: no texture, no glint, no rim. The pen is clear of the sheet by at least 22 mm.

8. The screen: in this checkout it is still the 1280x720 frame from 07:54, with pale keys and a blotchy bezel, so I scored it as it is. Your 2560 version with corners (64abcff) is on the remote branch and goes to the next review.

fixes.problem:
A soft shadow wedge darkens document_left's top-left corner:
- Raw luma is 152 at 5x5 mm in, against 191 at 30x30 mm and about 197-204 farther in.
- The 3 mm/20 mm ratio is 0.918 at the top edge and 0.938 on the left edge.

The code's geometry points to the soft edge of the spot cone:
- SPOT has no 'plate' entry, so set_lamp() gives pair (and page) the 72-degree, blend-0.70 cone.
- That cone is at full strength only within about 19.5 degrees of its axis.
- From the bulb at about (-0.29, 0.16, 0.41 m above the table), this corner is about 29 degrees off the axis, at roughly 0.45 strength. Every other corner of both sheets is within about 25 degrees.

Separately, a dark rounded shape with a curved edge fills the frame's top-left corner:
- The wood there is raw 25-30, against about 37-53 elsewhere.
- The lamp base at (-0.35, 0.20) sits just outside that corner of the frame. apply_camera() hides the lamp meshes from the camera for 'plate', but they still cast shadows, so the camera sees the dark table under the base.

A pinned letterhead would sit in a dim wedge that has no visible source.
fixes.fix:
1. In apply_camera(), take the lamp meshes out of the plate render. In the loop over _STATE['lamp'].children_recursive, set ob.hide_render = plate, or at least set visible_shadow and visible_diffuse to not plate. This removes the base's arc.
2. Widen the cone for pair only:
   - set_lamp() picks the cone by beat, and page shares the 'plate' beat, so changing SPOT would change page too.
   - Add a per-camera override instead, for example a 'spot' entry in CAMERAS['pair'] that apply_camera() applies to lamp_spot after set_beat().
   - Use about 88 degrees with blend 0.6. By the code's geometry that brings every corner of both sheets to about 0.97 of full cone strength or more.
   - Do not move the lamp mark instead. At about (-0.46, 0.27, -128) the cone edge lands on document_right's top-right corner (about 0.5 strength).
3. Keep exposure at -1.22 and check that the left sheet's raw centre stays at about 197-204.
4. Re-render pair at 2560x1440.
5. Targets on the raw frame:
   - document_left at (5 mm, 5 mm) is at least 0.92 of its value at (30 mm, 30 mm). It is 0.80 now.
   - Every 3 mm/20 mm station on both sheets is within 0.97-1.03.
   - The frame's top-left 200 px shows smooth falloff, with no curved edge.
6. Re-export pair.corners.json and pair.mask.png from the same render.

fixes.problem:
Paper and wood never meet in a contact shadow. Where the wood 10 mm out is clear of the other sheet, the wood 1 mm outside each edge is 0.81-1.16 of it. There is no consistent hairline shadow on the edges away from the lamp (right and bottom), so both sheets look like cards pasted on.

- the lamp's cone_haze box (density up to 0.055). At pair's lamp mark it is centred at about (-0.12, 0.06), so its dense core sits over document_left.

set_beat() hides neither of them for 'plate'. A multiplied page darkens that haze along with the paper, so ink will look slightly too black for the haze in front of it.
fixes.fix:

   - Aim for a 1-2 px hairline shadow on the wood, at 0.85-0.92 of the nearby wood, along the right and bottom edges.

2. In apply_camera(), when plate is true:

   Then adjust exposure so the left sheet's raw centre stays at about 197-204.
